technicalPrinciples.title: How JPG to WebP Conversion Works
technicalPrinciples.description: Understanding the technical advantages of WebP over JPG

items.title: Advanced Compression Technology
items.description: WebP uses VP8/VP9 predictive coding instead of JPG's DCT, achieving 25-35% better compression at same quality through advanced block prediction and entropy coding.

items.title: Quality Preservation
items.description: Converting JPG to WebP can maintain or improve perceived quality. WebP's advanced algorithms handle compression artifacts better, especially in gradients and textures.

items.title: Transparency Addition
items.description: Unlike JPG, WebP supports alpha channel transparency. While conversion doesn't add transparency automatically, the format enables future editing with transparency support.

items.title: Flexible Quality Control
items.description: WebP offers fine-grained quality control (0-100) with better quality-to-size ratio than JPG. Same quality as JPG at 25-35% smaller size, or better quality at same size.

items.content: WebP maintains photo quality while reducing bandwidth. Use quality 85-90 for portfolio photos (better than JPG 90-95 at smaller size). items.title: Cloud Storage & CDN
items.content: Converting JPG to WebP reduces cloud storage and CDN costs by 25-35%. Batch convert entire photo libraries for immediate savings. Use quality 80-85 for general content, 85-90 for premium content. Monitor browser support (95%+) and serve WebP to supported browsers, JPG to legacy. ROI is significant for high-traffic sites.

items.title: News & Content Sites
items.description: Improve page load speed and user engagement.
items.content: WebP reduces article image sizes by 25-35%, improving page load speed and SEO rankings. Convert featured images and inline photos to WebP (quality 80-85). items.title: When to Keep JPG
items.description: Scenarios where JPG is still the better choice.
items.content: Keep JPG if: 1) Need universal compatibility (emails, older systems), 2) Targeting Safari <14 or Chrome <85 users (check analytics), 3) Working with print workflows, 4) Client deliverables requiring JPG format. WebP excels for modern web apps with 95%+ browser support. Use progressive enhancement: WebP → JPG fallback.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about JPG to WebP conversion

items.question: Will converting JPG to WebP improve image quality?
items.answer: Converting JPG to WebP won't restore quality lost in original JPG compression, but WebP's advanced algorithms can maintain or improve perceived quality. At the same file size, WebP often looks better than JPG due to superior compression technology. For best results, convert from highest quality JPG available. WebP's better gradient handling reduces banding and blocking artifacts.

items.question: How much smaller are WebP files compared to JPG?
items.answer: WebP provides 25-35% better compression than JPG at equivalent quality. For example, a 1MB JPG photo might become 650-750KB as WebP with same visual quality. Actual savings depend on image content - photos with gradients and textures see better compression. You can also choose better quality at same size, or same quality at smaller size.

items.question: Which browsers support WebP format?
items.answer: WebP has 95%+ browser support as of 2024. Supported by Chrome 23+ (2012), Firefox 65+ (2019), Edge 18+ (2018), Safari 14+ (2020), and Opera 12.1+ (2012). Mobile support includes Chrome Android, Safari iOS 14+, and Samsung Internet 4+. For older browsers, implement <picture> element with WebP primary and JPG fallback.

items.question: Can I convert JPG to WebP without quality loss?
items.answer: Since JPG is already lossy, converting to WebP preserves current quality but cannot restore data lost in original JPG compression. For best results: 1) Convert from highest quality JPG, 2) Use WebP quality 80-90 to match or exceed JPG quality, 3) Compare visually before deploying. WebP's lossless mode is available but results in larger files than lossy WebP.

items.question: Should I convert all JPG images to WebP?
items.answer: For modern websites, yes - WebP provides significant performance benefits with 95%+ browser support. However: 1) Implement progressive enhancement (WebP → JPG fallback), 2) Keep JPG for emails and universal compatibility, 3) Monitor your audience's browser support, 4) Use quality 80-85 for general content. WebP is ideal for sites prioritizing performance and modern browser support.

items.question: Is JPG to WebP conversion free and secure?
items.answer: Yes, our JPG to WebP converter is completely free with no registration, watermarks, or payment required. All conversion happens locally in your browser using WebAssembly - your images never leave your device. This ensures 100% privacy and security, with no server uploads, data collection, or third-party access. WebP encoding is performed entirely client-side.
